subject: Node throttling event in reserved pool — immediate mitigations and follow-up
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@applify-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Node throttling event in reserved pool — immediate mitigations and follow-up

Samir —

Quick update from the ops side: at 08:12 PDT our telemetry flagged sustained token-serve latency on your us-west reserved pool (pool-id: rp-applify-usw-3). The symptoms were consistent with a node-level throttling path: several GPUs entered a slow-path due to an NVLINK contention we only observe under heavy small-batch traffic. The autoscaler misinterpreted the short, bursty traffic (many short requests under 128 tokens) and did not trigger additional warm nodes in time, which caused headroom exhaustion and increased queuing latency for ~18 minutes.

What we did immediately:
- Took the affected nodes out of rotation at 08:20 and moved active traffic to warm standby variants (manual routing).
- Manually added 2 reserved nodes to the pool at 08:24 to restore buffer capacity.
- Enabled an interim rule to force the autoscaler to consider short-batch QPS (hot-path) for 24h while we patch the prediction logic.

Customer impact: token latency increase for ~18 minutes (observable slowdown in synchronous generation calls). No data loss. Some clients observed 5–12s tail latency spikes; p95 remained within SLO after mitigation.

Next steps (we will follow up with a formal postmortem):
1) Engineering (Karthik) will triage logs and provide a root-cause write-up and a patch plan (ETA: 72 hours).
2) We will supply you with ops logs and a credit proposal for impacted window.
3) CS (Neha) and I will coordinate a short post-incident call if you'd like to review details live.

Attachments: ops-log-20280628.tar.gz (trimmed capture of pool telemetry and autoscaler decisions).

I'm looping Ben on credits and contract impacts. Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@applify-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: root cause summary, remediation plan, and credit offer

Samir —

Thanks again for your patience this morning. Below is a concise post-incident summary and the concrete items we are delivering to Applify Retail.

Summary of event (timeline):
- 08:12 PDT: telemetry alert — increasing per-request latency and queuing in rp-applify-usw-3.
- 08:20: removed two affected nodes from rotation; moved traffic to warm-standby routing.
- 08:24: manually provisioned +2 reserved nodes to restore headroom.
- 08:38: queue drain and p99 tail began to recover; by 08:52 full restoration observed. Total customer-facing impact window: ~18 minutes (08:12–08:30, conservative).

Root cause (engineering summary):
- Trigger: a burst of many small (<=128 token) synchronous requests created a hot-path workload.
- Autoscaler gap: the autoscaler bases decisions largely on average token throughput and warm-start latency; short bursts temporarily under-indexed the need for extra nodes.
- Node slow-path: the combination of small-batch NVLINK contention and a kernel scheduling fallback caused per-GPU execution to slow under those specific conditions.

Remediation (what we are doing now):
1) Immediate (complete): manual node add + routing to warm standby (already executed).
2) Short-term (ETA 72 hours): deploy autoscaler change to include short-batch QPS metric and adjust thresholding for warm-node injection. Will ship a canary to 10% of reserved pools before broad rollout.
3) Medium-term (2–3 weeks): kernel fallback adjustments and NVLINK scheduling optimization in the serving runtime to avoid the slow-path for the observed pattern.
4) Preventative: we will add a synthetic short-burst test to our canary suite to surface regressions.

Customer-facing remediation and offer:
- Credit: Redwood proposes a credit equal to 10% of the prorated June reserved fee for the impacted minutes (attachment: credit-offer-APPLIFY-20280628.pdf). Ben & Neha have prepared the customer note and invoice offset mechanics.
- Ops evidence: attached ops-log-20280628.tar.gz (truncated) with pool telemetry, autoscaler decisions, and node-level traces.

Requested actions for Applify Retail:
- Please confirm receipt and acceptance of the proposed credit by reply to this thread.
- If you’d like a walk-through of the logs and engineering plan, we’d be happy to schedule a 30-minute session this week.

Rough answers to your earlier questions:
- Exact credit window: conservative impact window used is 08:12–08:30 PDT (18 minutes). We included the buffer for diagnosis and routing.
- Reoccurrence risk for peak events: low after the short-term autoscaler change and medium-term kernel tweak; we will prioritize the Sept rehearsal to validate (we will coordinate a soak test ahead of your Black Friday run).
- Downstream retry guidance: if your services observe retries, adding small exponential backoff and jitter during known recovery intervals helps. We can provide recommended client-side retry knobs if you want an ops playbook.

Next steps for us: Karthik will share the engineering RCA doc (ETA 72 hours) and a rollout timetable for the autoscaler canary. Neha will send the official credit note and invoice instructions. Ben and I will remain your contacts for commercial and operational follow-up.

Apologies again for the disruption; we know reliability is foundational and appreciate the trust of the Applify team.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
